title: Pasted right-derived unit of a normalized direct-image square
statement: Fix schemes X,Y,X′,Y′ [def-pc-scheme] and common-universe derived module categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Let f:X→Y, f′:X′→Y′, g:Y′→Y and gX:X′→X satisfy h:gX;f=f′;g. The ordinary square e₀ is pushforwardComp(gX,f), pushforwardCongr(h), and inverse pushforwardComp(f′,g). The derived square e is schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso(gX,f), equality transport along h and inverse schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso(f′,g), with comparisons fixed by [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition]. Let U(A,B) denote the pasted right-derived unit of A followed by B. Then U(gX_*,f_*);Qh(e.hom)=Qh(e₀.hom);U(f′_*,g_*). This concerns only direct-image unit normalization. It has no open restriction, no pullback adjunction, and no mate or projection-counit conclusion.

proof.text: Apply the fixed composition-unit normalization theorem to the two paths, obtaining h₁ and h₂ for the two normalized comparisons.
Apply directImageSquare_unit_transport to obtain the equality-transport equation for the single direct-image unit.
Use the component assembly theorem to paste h₁, h₂ and the transport equation; natural-transformation extensionality gives the displayed equality.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedDirectImageSquare_unit
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (gX : X' ⟶ X)
    (h : gX ≫ f = f' ≫ g) :
    let e₀ := Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp gX f ≪≫
      Scheme.Modules.pushforwardCongr h ≪≫ (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp f' g).symm
    let e := schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso gX f ≪≫
      eqToIso (congrArg (fun t ↦ schemeDerivedDirectImage t) h) ≪≫
      (schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso f' g).symm
    Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompUnit (Scheme.Modules.pushforward gX)
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f) ≫
      Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh e.hom =
    Functor.whiskerRight (NatTrans.mapHomotopyCategory e₀.hom (.up ℤ))
      DerivedCategory.Qh ≫
      Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompUnit (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f')
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward g)
